title: Dynamic kernel matcher for conversational burst isolation
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: conversational workloads show bursty token patterns (short interactive turns followed by long completions). Our current static kernel pickers either optimize for steady-state throughput (good for long-decode) or for single-request latency (good for short prefill), but they frequently misallocate kernels at phase boundaries, causing p95/p99 latency spikes and higher unit-cost during bursts.

Goal: implement a dynamic kernel matcher that detects conversational phases (prefill vs decode vs burst tail) and performs a lightweight, phase-conditioned kernel handoff with online autotuning. The matcher should: 1) minimize end-to-end tail latency for interactive sessions, 2) avoid unnecessary full-model warmstarts when switching kernels, and 3) maintain or improve per-token cost compared to today.

Scope: runtime patch + scheduler integration, small microbenchmark harness, canary rollout behind flag, and A/B metrics pipeline for latency/cost/regression checks.
acceptance_criteria: Phase detector flags prefill/decode/burst with >90% precision on held-out conversational traces
End-to-end p99 latency improvement >= 15% for mixed conversational workload in canary traffic
No more than 3% increase in per-token unit cost on average across sampled workloads
Kernel handoff latency (additional overhead) < 2ms for warmstart-free switches
Autotuner converges within 1 hour of mixed traffic for common GPU families (A100/H100-equivalents)
steps: Design: define phase taxonomy and lightweight features (recent token counts, KV cache growth, logits variance, user idle time)
Prototype: implement matcher as a pluggable policy in runtime with simulated trace replayer
Autotune infra: add probe sampler that executes candidate kernel pairs on short warmup windows and records cost/latency
Integrate with prefill/decode scheduler: pre-declare transitions to avoid redundant cache transfers
Benchmark: microbench on heterogeneous GPU pool, compare against baseline kernel picker across seqlen distributions
Canary rollout: feature flag + 1% traffic -> 10% -> 50% with automated rollback on SLO regressions
Postmortem & docs: publish playbook for extending to new architectures and quantized kernels
comments: 2026-02-22 - Aisha Patel: Kicked off design doc. Initial feature set focuses on short metadata (last 64 tokens, user inter-arrival time) to keep cost low. Decided to avoid heavyweight ML models for phase detection in first iteration.

2026-02-27 - Marco Chen: Prototype integrated with scheduler; discovered 8ms overhead when we performed a full KV handoff between incompatible kernels. Plan: implement warmstart-friendly intermediate buffer and metadata-only handshake to avoid copying unless absolutely necessary.
2026-03-02 - Elena Rivera (PM): Prioritized canary metrics. Added p95 and p99 SLO gates and a cost delta monitor. Requested that the autotuner maintain historical rollbacks for at least 24 hours.

2026-03-04 - Marco Chen: Implemented probe sampler. Early results on H100-equivalent nodes: phase-aware selection reduces p99 by ~18% on mixed sessions, but increased average token-cost by 2.6% — within target. Observed two failure modes where short bursts oscillated kernel choices; added hysteresis and minimum dwell time of 3s.

2026-03-07 - Design review (Noah Singh): UX for rollout controls in Console: add toggle for 'Aggressive handoff' and a visualization showing phase transition events per user session. Design approved with minor label changes.

2026-03-09 - QA (Priya Das): Regression suite ran 1200 conversational traces. Phase detector precision = 92.3% on holdout. One flaky failure reproduces on older A100 drivers; create ENG-612346 to track driver/allocator issue.
2026-03-10 - Marco Chen: Preparing canary PR and traffic plan. Need infra team approval for 1% traffic canary on dedicated pools. Filed infra request (INFRA-9032).
notes: Key trade-offs: keep phase detector stateless and low-cost to avoid introducing new performance regressions; accept small short-term cost uptick for significant tail-latency improvements. Future work: extend autotuner to include quantized kernels and multi-arch policy matrices.
